C0000.summary: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including how the disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum, for preschool children (as appropriate) how it affects participation in appropriate activities, and for children with disabilities taking alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, benchmarks or short-term objectives; (II) measurable annual goals (including academic and functional goals) designed to meet needs resulting from the disability to enable involvement and progress in the general education curriculum and meet each other educational need resulting from the disability; (III) a description of how progress toward meeting annual goals will be measured and when periodic progress reports (such as quarterly or other periodic reports, concurrent with report cards) will be provided; (IV) a statement of special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services (based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable), and program modifications or supports for school personnel, to advance appropriately toward annual goals, be involved and make progress in the general education curriculum, participate in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children; (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in regular class and such activities; (VI) a statement of individual appropriate accommodations necessary to measure academic achievement and functional performance on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A), and if the IEP Team determines the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment and why the alternate assessment selected is appropriate; (VII) the projected start date for services and modifications, and their anticipated frequency, location, and duration; and (VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the child is 16 (updated annually), appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based on age-appropriate transition assessments and transition services needed to assist in reaching them, plus (beginning not later than 1 year before reaching the age of majority under State law) a statement that the child has been informed of rights under this chapter, if any, transferring on reaching majority under section 1415(m).

C0001.summary: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require that additional information be included in a child’s IEP beyond what is explicitly required in this section.

C0002.summary: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require the IEP Team to include information under 1 component of a child’s IEP that is already contained under another component of such IEP.

C0003.summary: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program team” or “IEP Team” means a group of individuals composed of: (i) the parents of a child with a disability; (ii) not less than 1 regular education teacher of such child (if the child is, or may be, participating in the regular education environment); (iii) not less than 1 special education teacher, or where appropriate, not less than 1 special education provider of such child; (iv) a representative of the local educational agency who is qualified to provide, or supervise the provision of, specially designed instruction to meet the unique needs of children with disabilities, is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum, and is knowledgeable about the availability of resources of the local educational agency; (v) an individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results, who may be a member of the team described in clauses (ii) through (vi); (vi) at the discretion of the parent or the agency, other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the child, including related services personnel as appropriate; and (vii) whenever appropriate, the child with a disability.

C0004.summary: A member of the IEP Team shall not be required to attend an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, if the parent of a child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that the attendance of such member is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting.
C0004.scope_text: if the parent of a child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that the attendance of such member is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting

C0005.summary: A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal, and the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.
C0005.scope_text: when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal, and the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting

C0006.summary: A parent’s agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing.

C0007.summary: In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, an invitation to the initial IEP meeting shall, at the request of the parent, be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator or other representatives of the subchapter III system to assist with the smooth transition of services.
C0007.scope_text: In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, at the request of the parent

inventory.U0000: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with section 1414 and that includes the required statutory components.
inventory.U0001: An IEP must include a statement of the child's present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including how the child’s disability affects the child’s involvement and progress in the general education curriculum.
inventory.U0002: For preschool children, an IEP must include a statement, as appropriate, of how the disability affects the child’s participation in appropriate activities as part of the child's present levels of academic achievement and functional performance.
inventory.U0003: For children with disabilities who take alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, an IEP must include a description of benchmarks or short-term objectives as part of the present levels statement.
inventory.U0004: An IEP must include a statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals, designed to meet the child’s needs resulting from the disability to enable the child to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum, and to meet each of the child’s other educational needs resulting from the disability.
inventory.U0005: An IEP must include a description of how the child’s progress toward meeting the annual goals will be measured, and a description of when periodic reports on the progress the child is making toward meeting those goals (such as through quarterly or other periodic reports concurrent with report cards) will be provided.
inventory.U0006: An IEP must include a statement of the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services (based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable) to be provided to the child or on behalf of the child, and a statement of program modifications or supports for school personnel provided for the child to advance appropriately toward attaining annual goals, to be involved and progress in the general education curriculum and participate in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and to be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children.
inventory.U0007: An IEP must include an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in the regular class and in the extracurricular and other nonacademic activities described in subclause (IV)(cc).
inventory.U0008: An IEP must include a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the child on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A).
inventory.U0009: If the IEP Team determines that the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, the IEP must include a statement of why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment and why the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate for the child.
inventory.U0010: An IEP must include the projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications described in subclause (IV), as well as their anticipated frequency, location, and duration.
inventory.U0011: Beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter, the IEP must include appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based upon age-appropriate transition assessments related to training, education, employment, and, where appropriate, independent living skills.
inventory.U0012: Beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter, the IEP must include the transition services (including courses of study) needed to assist the child in reaching the postsecondary goals.
inventory.U0013: Beginning not later than 1 year before the child reaches the age of majority under State law, the IEP must include a statement that the child has been informed of any rights under this chapter that will transfer to the child upon reaching the age of majority under section 1415(m).
inventory.U0014: Nothing in section 1414 shall be construed to require that additional information be included in a child’s IEP beyond what is explicitly required in this section.
inventory.U0015: Nothing in section 1414 shall be construed to require the IEP Team to include information under one component of a child’s IEP that is already contained under another component of that IEP.
inventory.U0016: The individualized education program team (IEP Team) includes the parents of a child with a disability.
inventory.U0017: The IEP Team includes not less than 1 regular education teacher of the child, if the child is, or may be, participating in the regular education environment.
inventory.U0018: The IEP Team includes not less than 1 special education teacher, or where appropriate, not less than 1 special education provider of the child.
inventory.U0019: The IEP Team includes a representative of the local educational agency who is qualified to provide or supervise specially designed instruction for children with disabilities, is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum, and is knowledgeable about the availability of agency resources.
inventory.U0020: The IEP Team includes an individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results, who may be an existing team member described in clauses (ii) through (vi).
inventory.U0021: At the discretion of the parent or the agency, the IEP Team may include other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the child, including related services personnel as appropriate.
inventory.U0022: Whenever appropriate, the IEP Team includes the child with a disability.
inventory.U0023: A member of the IEP Team is not required to attend an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, if the parent of the child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that attendance is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting.
inventory.U0024: A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal and the member submits written input into the development of the IEP to the parent and the IEP Team prior to the meeting.
inventory.U0025: A parent’s agreement to an IEP Team member not attending an IEP meeting under clause (i) and a parent's consent to an IEP Team member excusal under clause (ii) must be in writing.
inventory.U0026: In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, an invitation to the initial IEP meeting shall, at the request of the parent, be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator or other representatives of the subchapter III system to assist with the smooth transition of services.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 comprehensively and accurately defines an 'individualized education program' or 'IEP' in accordance with 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A), preserving each statutory element from (I) through (VIII), along with their internal qualifiers, age thresholds, and cross-references.

Claim C0001 faithfully states the rule of construction under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii)(I) providing that nothing in this section requires additional information in an IEP beyond what is explicitly required.

Claim C0002 accurately captures the rule of construction under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii)(II) that the IEP Team is not required to include information under one component of an IEP that is already contained under another component.

Claim C0003 accurately defines the 'individualized education program team' or 'IEP Team' pursuant to 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(B), faithfully including all required members, conditions, qualifications, and discretionary components.

Claim C0004 correctly conveys the attendance exception under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(i), establishing when an IEP Team member is not required to attend an IEP meeting based on parental and agency agreement.

Claim C0005 faithfully reflects 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(ii) permitting an IEP Team member to be excused from attending a meeting when their area is modified or discussed, provided there is consent and prior written input.
Claim C0006 accurately represents the statutory requirement in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(iii) that a parent's agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) must be in writing.

Claim C0007 accurately states the mandate under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(D) to send an invitation to the initial IEP meeting to subchapter III representatives upon parental request for children previously served under subchapter III.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 fully covers the general definition of an IEP under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(i).

Claim C0000 includes the requirement of benchmarks or short-term objectives for children taking alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards.
Claim C0000 preserves the requirement for measurable annual goals (academic and functional) designed to meet needs resulting from the disability.
Claim C0000 incorporates the requirement to describe how progress will be measured and when periodic progress reports will be provided.
Claim C0000 preserves the requirement for statements of special education, related services, supplementary aids, and program modifications or supports.
Claim C0000 preserves the requirement for an explanation of the extent to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children.
Claim C0000 retains the requirement for a statement of individual appropriate accommodations on State and districtwide assessments.
Claim C0000 includes the required explanations when an alternate assessment is selected.
Claim C0000 retains the requirement for the projected start date, frequency, location, and duration of services and modifications.
Claim C0000 includes the requirement for postsecondary transition goals beginning not later than when the child is 16.
Claim C0000 preserves the requirement for transition services needed to assist in reaching postsecondary goals.
Claim C0000 includes the statement of rights transfer beginning not later than 1 year before reaching majority.
Claim C0001 faithfully preserves the rule of construction regarding additional information in the IEP.
Claim C0002 faithfully preserves the rule of construction prohibiting requiring duplicative IEP component information.
Claim C0003 includes the child's parents in the IEP Team composition.
Claim C0003 includes the regular education teacher requirement and its governing condition.
Claim C0003 includes the special education teacher or provider requirement.
Claim C0003 includes the qualifications and knowledge requirements for the LEA representative.
Claim C0003 includes the individual who can interpret evaluation results and notes they may be an existing team member.
Claim C0003 preserves the discretionary inclusion of other individuals with knowledge or expertise.
Claim C0003 retains the provision regarding participation of the child with a disability whenever appropriate.
Claim C0004 fully retains the statutory exception for non-attendance when an area is not modified or discussed.
Claim C0005 fully retains the excusal rules, including consent and written input prior to the meeting.
